## Wakt 1.0.7

### Browsers can no longer sidestep the website filter with their own DNS
The DNS log from 1.0.6 showed the real culprit: Chrome's built-in "secure DNS" (DNS over HTTPS to Cloudflare). Chrome asked system DNS only for `chrome.cloudflare-dns.com`, then sent every site lookup over HTTPS straight to Cloudflare, so the filter never saw facebook or any other blocked site.

- Lookups for the DoH resolvers built into Chrome, Firefox, Edge, Brave and others are now refused (NXDOMAIN). Firefox's `use-application-dns.net` canary is included, which tells Firefox to switch DoH off on this network.
- The well-known public resolver addresses (Cloudflare, Google, Quad9, OpenDNS, CleanBrowsing, AdGuard, ControlD) are routed into the tunnel. Plain DNS to them is still answered; TCP connections to them (DoH, DoT) are reset immediately so the browser fails fast and falls back to system DNS, where the blocks apply.
- The website-filter card warns when an app was caught trying to use its own encrypted DNS, naming the app and resolver. These lookups show as BLOCKED-DOH in the DNS log.

### If Chrome then shows "DNS error" on every site
That means Chrome's secure DNS is set to a specific provider rather than automatic, so it refuses to fall back. Turn it off once: Chrome menu, Settings, Privacy and security, Use secure DNS, Off.
